comments.value: This is very reasonable. I agree!

1. These "bypass" systems are not valid. Using the new scaling system world creators can Limit the size aswell using Udon. Meaning regardless of avatar default size it will forcefully scale down the avatar if avatar's needed. However, I do feel like if the world is Private and NOT a game world tagged with #game then it should be automatically enabled as it is a private. https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/no-limit-to-avatar-scaling-in-invite-invite-friends-friends-worlds

2. You need to keep in mind VRChat is not made for these "big avatars" and that goes for all game engines, not just VRChat and unity. Going too big can break UI elements and cause unwanted behavior and rendering fragmints (can be viewed by large worlds like flight sims)... it's best to limit it to a dagree. You could also argue that VRChat avatar creators should have control. They do. They have a "defualt size" and unless udon forced into a size will remain the same size. The world control is just to allow world creators to "limit" said size. For example, when playing Murder its very annoying for someone to be big, or small. In this case it would be nice to force everyone to the same hight so no one needs to change avatars and everyone is happy.

3. The method used for Avatar side scaling is "buggy" and a weird work around. This is why Gogo Loco Scale was called "GoGo **Broke**". And beacuse it isn't supported natively can cause issues with VRChat.

@{619ffdfe00e2a864e7efb2e1|full_name}: All i want is that the way we currently have scaling work (using GOGO Loco) is the way this should be addressed. There's already systems in VRC to deal with people abusing these option like Kicking , blocking or upping your security levels. Having you (the world author) decide what i can use and makes it feel so bad. The fact that things like the ui break at certain scale is fine as there is ways to reset and it's also not supported by vrc. they even mention it in the upload window of Unity. But that doesn't mean i can't do it, just means i might encounter issues and have to deal with it... but at least i can be tiny or big where ever i want.

Because it allows creators to build systems like this, it should not.

https://vxtwitter.com/hotaru86_VR/status/1672878167101698048?s=20

If we're talking about tools that could be used to experience a world in a way unintended by the author, one of the biggest addons for VR (OVR Advanced Settings) can easily disrupt any experience through it's ability to clip your viewpoint anywhere with playspace mover (you can literally drag yourself through a wall to grab an item in an adventure world or engage some sort of trigger). Avi Scaling is no different imo and putting a limit on it is kinda silly.

Honestly there's a bigger conversation to be had about accessibility settings be limited due to wanting worlds to be experienced 'as intended' (limiting the bloom feature, inability to toggle off/adjust post-processing, etc). 

Good chunk of requested features allow users to better to engage with content and for a good part of things don't effect anyone's experience but their own.

To add to this, having worlds control avatar size is a consent issue. If worlds can adjust my size without my consent, i will be afraid to go explore new worlds. Right now I control my own avatar. Worlds can be a bad experience sometimes, but i am always safe in being myself wherever i go. This changes that. The world can do something to me that i do not want, not just changing my surroundings but actually affecting me personally. 

People should at least be able to disable worlds scaling them as an accessibility setting, for people who do not consent to that, or who cant handle the motion sickness of potential size changes.

@{5f2d2f4df6abbf61555a67b7|full_name}: Okay, to clarify if your playing a game on roblox are you going to get upset about your Roblox identity because a game changed your size? It's not like its forcing you into a whole other avatar. I have some friends that are still trying to figure out their identity's, or have chosen one for themselves. Size is never an issue with this matter, and its about the person. If you have a complain about your identity in a public world you enjoy, feel free to contact the world creator and beg them to change it. Personally, regardless of how you identity in height, it's still annoying in some worlds to be overly small or tall.

@{619ffdfe00e2a864e7efb2e1|full_name}: Roblox is irrelevant. People arent getting phantom sense in Roblox (i imagine anyway, ive never played). I dont think people in roblox feel pain if someone hits them.

Just because size doesnt matter to you personally, is no sort of indicator of how other people feel about size. It matters for me, and im asking you to accept that i am telling the truth about my experience, and about the experience of other people i know. Not everyone is like you.

You might be annoyed by someone being taller or smaller than you prefer, but on my end if my size is changed without my consent i might have a panic attack and not be able to be in vr for several days. These are very different reactions and one is certainly more serious than the other.

If your comment was that you would feel annoyed if you were the wrong size for the world, rather than a comment on other people? Then you could change your size to fit the world if scaling was an avatar decision rather than a world decision because you could always have control over that. Thats what i would like to be doing, i want to choose my scale so that i fit the world and fit the height of my friends, in every world. Just as i do now.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: i have been informed that the option is going to be on by default. I understand the change but it doesnt really adress my biggest issue with the system. Preventing scaling in a world, let's say mine because I don't want my model to breakdie to particles, parent constraints and other systems not working after scaling, also prevents everyone from using scale on their own models...which I do not want. I want people to be able to scale their own stuff if they want to just not scale mine since i didnt make them with that in mind. If they scale them later, they would have a less then great experience since the effects and items made for the models would have bad placements and size once scaled. Some shaders that use dissolve are the most affected right now. I dont want to have to redo all the models i ever made just so they dont break when using scaling. I would prefer having the option to scale implemented on models that i want to be able to scale. I know you guys are working hard at implementing this option but i still think its getting implemented in the wrong way.

having scaling built into vrc the way it is now in the latest beta is neat, i would just like if you could clientside define the range for any world, that doesn't explicitly defines a range. 

I think that would be the optimal solution

Update: As of testing today, 7/19/23, it seems that IK targets are scaling with avatars, or at least aren't breaking horribly in my particular use case. I still have concerns about the feature, but at least my particular collection of avatars do not seem to be currently broken.

I still struggle to see why worlds should even be taken into consideration when they were not previously. Introducing world control of scaling is injecting a user consent and personal comfort problem where there previously was none.

@{5f2d2f4df6abbf61555a67b7|full_name}: Yes, that's right.

Changing the avatar size from the world should require permission from the user, and there should be a way to disable it without navigating through menus, such as panic mode.

It can not be said that there is no abuse of gimmicks as pasted below.

https://twitter.com/Noch3d/status/1672781352045871105

I want to support creative freedom and say there are already systems in place to combat tall or tiny avatar griefers. It also doesn't stop them from using a defaulty small or big avatar. As for scaling breaking world UIs, the issue is self solving and the player will usually change to a normal avatar to experience the world as intended after running into errors. But as an accessibility or quality of life feature, it seems very frustrating and jarring if you go world to world, changing heights against your will. Also a small thought, I'm sorry but I think everyone is just going to abuse it and we will see an uptick in annoying avatar sizes if it's on by default. Lastly, I've never seen gogo used maliciously, it's always avatars that are already tall.

@{642640977e532309f8e5b7ca|full_name}: So much agreed on the user consent and personal comfort problem. I felt genuinely angry the first time I logged into LS Media and was hard denied from being taller than 2 meters. I feel like part of my identity has been stripped from me. My avatar's default eye height is 2.28m because I like to "be the couch" and have people rest on me. Being slightly too big for whatever world I'm in is something I'm used to and it makes me more comfortable because being big lets people rest on me. Which makes me feel important and appreciated. I am upset that this was taken away from me.

details:
With the "New" scaling system implemented in the Beta build, I'm left displease and pretty let down by the choices and direction taken with the feature. Here's a few point I think they should address before making this feature available at all. 

1: Make the feature an system or option for avatar makers, not world makers : 

As is stands now in the beta, the only option is to have the world author allow or code in (UDON) the system. This means it limits usage to only sdk3 worlds and world that are still maintained by their creators. This was said to be done so people would not abuse scaling in maps that don't want you to. I think this is a bad way of limiting players in VRC. You can still make tall models that exceed a worlds recommended size. There are many other ways to abuse game worlds with the tool vrc already provides so i don't see the issue here. 

2:  Avatars cannot grow to be very tall : I like many other people like to sometimes be a giant model. The sense of scale and interactions with smaller other people is fun and I want to keep that. This scaling system locked people to a 5meter height and even breaks avatars that are taller to become 5 meters maximum. This is an issue. If people don't want to see a giant model, the safety system is there for that specific reason. Not everyone can code UDON to make the ranges higher.... and not all models will be made to support scaling feature. Having it be like it already is with GOGO loco, you can create your model to support it if you want to. Have it be a model option and not a world option.... which brings me to...

3: GOGO Loco breaking on purpose: VRC mentionned it in their document that is was a “by design” break. Since world authors are in control, they don't want the avatar author to be able to scale their own models. This is, for a lack of a better word, stupid as hell. I make models and I don't make them scale with gogo or with vrc because some issues remained with parent constraint. HAVING SAID THAT I would not prevent people from scaling their own models. If they have the system on their avatar go right ahead! 

There are other reasons but mostly this is why i think they should rethink their approach and that avatar scaling should remain a system that is avatar based and not world based.
title: Scaling should remain an Avatar Feature and not a World Feature.
